To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have formalized two different perspectives on the notion of sociomataterial entanglement; (2) we have shown that the second perspective, the agential realist one, is more challenging for the purposes of formal knowledge representation; (3) we have proposed a solution to the challenge, by introducing the notion of information modules.

(1) the critical realist perspective on sociomaterial entangled systems can be modeled by means of a modular ontology, and (2) the agential realist perspective on the same systems requires the use of an ontology that is itself entangled.

(1) the notion of socio-technical systems as entangled can be modeled as a property of an already given ontological model of the world; (2) the distinction between ontological and informational entanglement can be modeled as the distinction between a property of the world and a property of the knowledge of the world; and (3) the distinction of information into ontological modules can be modeled as an epistemological entangled reality.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a formal ontology of socio-technical systems, which is able to account for the entangled nature of reality, and with the formal representation of the assumptions that are at the basis of such an ontology.
the development of a formal framework for the representation of sociomaterial systems and their evolution.
the conceptualization of sociomaterial reality and its representation in a formal ontology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the critical realist approach to sociomateriality is more suitable to the formalization of the concept of entanglement in the context of knowledge representation, while the agential realist approach is better suited to the description of the ontological status of sociomaterial entities.
, while the critical realist ontology of entanglement can be modeled by means of a formal ontology, the agential realist ontology of sociomaterial reality cannot.

the critical realist approach is a necessary condition to build a formal ontology of sociomaterial systems, while the agential realist perspective provides the necessary condition to make it possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to formalize the notion of entanglement in the context of a formal ontology and how to use it for modeling socio-technical systems.

we have proposed a conceptualization for sociomaterial entangle that is compatible with the critical realist approach and that can be formalized in a way compatible with the agential realist one, thus enabling the interoperability among the different views.

the critical realist perspective is more suitable for the description and representation of socio-technical systems, while the agential realist perspective is a promising candidate for their design and construction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
formal ontologies can be a valuable tool for modeling and analyzing socio-technical systems.
the critical and agential realist views on sociomateriality are not necessarily incompatible and can be reconciled in a knowledge representation framework.

the critical realist and agential realist approaches to the concept of sociomaterialism are not incompatible and that, on the contrary, they can be seen as complementary, as the former provides a conceptualization that is more amenable to knowledge representation while the latter offers a more general perspective on the notion of entanglement.
